summary:
Held 0 of today's 10 biggest US movers.

• 6 upside misses — LITE +11%, HPE +10%, SNDK +8%, NCLH +7%, LRCX +6%. These cleared the universe screen but no strategy picked them up; the morning brief either filtered them on a catalyst/RSI/earnings rule or had nothing positive to trigger an entry.

• 4 downside moves (APA -5%, PSKY -4%, COST -4%, CINF -3%) are unreachable on a long-only basket — no mechanism to express a short or pair-trade.

• Most instructive miss: LITE (+11.13%) — Leaked internal Meta memo showing plans to double AI compute to 14GW next year (plus custom AI chip entering production) ignited a fiber-optics/AI-networking rally; JPMorgan also reiterated Overweight, calling recent weakness a buying opportunity. Why we passed: Outside any active strategy's universe — Lumentum is classified as an optical-components/photonics industrial name, not tagged as AI-infrastructure/semiconductor, so momentum and news-reactive bots never scan it despite its ~700% 1yr AI-driven run and now-mega-cap size.

top_movers.catalyst: Leaked internal Meta memo showing plans to double AI compute to 14GW next year (plus custom AI chip entering production) ignited a fiber-optics/AI-networking rally; JPMorgan also reiterated Overweight, calling recent weakness a buying opportunity.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — Lumentum is classified as an optical-components/photonics industrial name, not tagged as AI-infrastructure/semiconductor, so momentum and news-reactive bots never scan it despite its ~700% 1yr AI-driven run and now-mega-cap size.
top_movers.suggestion: Add optical-networking/photonics names (LITE, COHR, FN) to the AI-infrastructure universe tag alongside semis, and refresh universe membership using rolling sector-momentum/market-cap screens rather than a static sector list.

top_movers.catalyst: Vultr picked HPE (with Nvidia GB300 NVL72 gear) to build large-scale AI data centers, adding to a ~$6B AI order backlog and fresh Q2/Juniper-integration momentum.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — HPE is a legacy enterprise-hardware/server OEM name, a category the bot's universes (built around semis/hyperscalers/pure AI-momentum names) likely don't cover despite its now-mega-cap AI-infrastructure exposure.
top_movers.suggestion: Add server-OEM/enterprise-hardware names with rising AI-infra order backlogs (e.g. HPE, DELL) to the AI-momentum strategy's universe screen based on backlog-growth or hyperscaler-deal keyword flags.

top_movers.catalyst: Multi-day short-covering rally on stacked analyst price-target hikes (Wells Fargo $19→$25, Citi $21→$25, Morgan Stanley $20→$22) plus falling oil prices easing cruise fuel-cost worries.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — NCLH is a ~$19, sub-$10B travel/leisure mid-cap with heavy short interest; likely excluded by a market-cap or sector-inclusion filter rather than a signal miss.
top_movers.suggestion: Add travel/leisure mid-caps (cruise operators) to the universe screen and add a short-interest-driven oversold-bounce trigger (5-session drawdown ≥10% + oil price reversal) to flag squeeze candidates pre-open.

top_movers.catalyst: Wave of analyst price-target hikes (Stifel to $425, TD Cowen/Mizuho to $400, Morgan Stanley to $404) on AI-driven memory-chip equipment demand, plus SK Hynix's $26.5B Nasdaq IPO.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe - LRCX is a mega-cap semi-equipment name. The move was a multi-day analyst-upgrade cascade, not a scheduled catalyst (earnings not until 7/29), so no news-reactive trigger applied either.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a sector-agnostic analyst-momentum trigger (>=3 price-target hikes + >=5% move over a rolling 5-day window) so names outside the static sector/ticker universe list can still surface.

top_movers.catalyst: Invesco released preliminary June AUM of $2,470.3B (+0.7% MoM), with $8.0B net long-term inflows and $14.3B money-market inflows, pre-market on 7/10.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — IVZ is a mid-cap (~$18-19B) traditional asset manager whose moves are driven by scheduled monthly AUM prints, not technical/momentum patterns the universe screens for.
top_movers.suggestion: Add asset-manager tickers to the news-reactive universe with a monthly-AUM-release calendar trigger (similar to earnings-gate) so a MoM AUM beat like +0.7% flags pre-market inclusion, not just quarterly earnings days.

top_movers.catalyst: Broad energy-sector selloff: WTI/Brent crude fell ~4% to multi-month lows as Hormuz tensions eased (tankers resuming transit, IEA data showing supply normalizing); Truist also issued a bearish note on APA on 7/10.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — APA is a mid-cap E&P/oil & gas explorer whose price action is dominated by commodity (WTI/Brent) beta rather than idiosyncratic, stock-specific catalysts, so it likely falls outside the equity universes the bot's momentum/news-reactive strategies are built to screen.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a macro-conditioned energy sub-universe keyed off daily WTI/Brent % change (e.g., include E&P names when sector ETF XOP moves >2%) so oil-beta-driven movers like APA become visible to a dedicated commodity-overlay strategy instead of being permanently filtered out.

top_movers.catalyst: Multi-state coalition prepping antitrust lawsuits to block the PSKY-WBD merger; Arete downgraded to Sell citing deal debt burden, forcing merger close to be pushed to July 22.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — PSKY is a sub-$10, recently-formed merger entity (Paramount+Skydance closed 2025) with a short listing history, likely below the market-cap/liquidity-track-record thresholds used for universe inclusion.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a merger-arb/deal-risk watchlist that admits active M&A-target tickers regardless of listing-age cutoff, so regulatory-driven gaps in newly merged names aren't structurally excluded from coverage.

top_movers.catalyst: June sales report: comp sales decelerated to 8.8% (from May's 12.5%) despite 10.6% net sales growth; analysts also flagged a modeled ~71% FY Q4 free-cash-flow drop from warehouse capex/tariff refund delays.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — COST is a mega-cap, low-beta consumer-staples retailer; the bot's universes screen for higher-beta/momentum names, so a staple with a scheduled monthly sales print never entered the candidate list.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a recurring monthly-sales-release calendar watch for staples/retail tickers (Costco-style same-store-sales prints) that can flag deceleration-driven moves even for names normally filtered out by low-beta/volatility screens.

top_movers.catalyst: Sell-side analyst downgraded CINF to 'Market Perform' with a trimmed price target, cited as overvalued near its recent all-time high (~$192 on 7/2); stock fell 3.38% on the rating cut.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe entirely — CINF is a staid, low-beta $28B P&C insurer, not the kind of high-momentum/liquid name these strategies track. A single analyst downgrade (not earnings/M&A) also isn't a signal type most news-reactive scanners are tuned to catch pre-move.
top_movers.suggestion: No actionable change — outside risk tolerance/universe design; large-cap low-beta insurers are intentionally excluded from momentum/news-reactive universes, and single-analyst rating actions are low-conviction, hard-to-front-run catalysts.
